_about: Host tool names the orchestration meter needs (sisi/orchestration.py). Per host: `delegation` tools start a worker (where the call carries the model and the brief text, as dotted paths into the tool's input); `exempt` tools are never counted as direct work (the question dialog, planning and to-do tools, messaging tools). Any other tool, including one named nowhere here, counts. `refuse` says how the host's before-tool hook refuses a call: `json-deny` prints the host's permission-deny JSON, `exit-2` exits with status 2 and the reason on standard error, `none` means the meter only counts there. `evidence` says how sure this entry is. `capability` tools list what the host can reach (providers and models, as dotted paths into the tool's result), and a delegation entry that names a `provider` path says where the call carries the provider; both carry `reach`, the label under which what they learn is stored (sisi/discovery.py, read through orchestration.reach_specs). A tool name here may be an exact name or, when it starts with `^`, a pattern. This file is the one description of a host's tools: sisi/orchestration.py and sisi/discovery.py both read it.
